BMCicada_A.overview:
The Cicada was introduced in 2740 by HartfordCo Industries, a small firm on Bryant whose previous manufacturing experience had been confined to communications and targeting systems. Designed as a supplement or replacement for the popular Locust scout 'Mech, the Cicada was built to compete directly with Bergan Industries' design by matching its speed while doubling its mass, allowing for improved weaponry and an edge in physical combat while keeping costs manageable.

The Star League found sufficient merit in the design to award HartfordCo a limited contract, using the Cicada to replace Locusts lost in fighting along border regions. Though the original factory on Bryant was destroyed during the Succession Wars, stockpiled Cicadas found their way into all five Successor State armies. Production was eventually revived by Free Worlds Defense Industries on Gibson, saving the design from extinction.
BMCicada_A.capabilities:
The Cicada's prime assets are its speed and freedom from ammunition concerns. A massive Pitban 320 engine, comprising more than half the 'Mech's total mass, propels the forty-ton chassis to speeds approaching 130 kilometers per hour. The standard armament of two medium lasers and one small laser provides sufficient firepower to engage lighter 'Mechs while eliminating logistical dependencies. The lasers are embedded in the armored torso behind the heaviest protection, though this placement creates limited firing arcs that an opponent can exploit by maneuvering behind the 'Mech.

The Cicada's four tons of armor matches that of the much lighter Locust, with the bulk concentrated in the torso. The vestigial arm assemblies and legs carry only minimal protection, making speed the design's primary defense. A well-documented flaw in the original HartfordCo heat sinks caused them to wear out and operate at only sixty percent capacity after extended use, leading to dangerous overheating in combat. While most surviving Cicadas have had their heat sinks replaced with reliable modular units, some examples with defective sinks remained in service until the Free Worlds League Military ordered a comprehensive upgrade program in 3029.
BMCicada_A.history:
HartfordCo Industries entered the BattleMech market in 2740 amid rising tensions throughout the Inner Sphere. The firm, already known for producing the Von Luckner heavy tank and various electronics packages, sought to challenge Bergan Industries' dominance in the light reconnaissance 'Mech market. The Star League's acceptance of the Cicada, though limited in scope, validated the design and established its reputation as a capable scout platform.

The fall of the Star League and destruction of HartfordCo's Bryant facility during the Succession Wars scattered existing Cicadas across the Inner Sphere. Bryant's central location made it a target for raids by all five Successor States, ensuring the design's widespread distribution. The 'Mech earned a positive reputation in service to the Successor Lords, though this sometimes led to expectations exceeding the design's actual capabilities. By the end of the Fourth Succession War, dwindling numbers threatened the Cicada with extinction.

The discovery of the Helm Memory Core allowed Free Worlds Defense Industries to resurrect production on Gibson, providing the Free Worlds League Military with desperately needed reconnaissance assets following losses in the Andurien conflict. The design proved an excellent platform for recovered lostech, leading to upgraded variants mounting extended-range weapons and improved electronics. Following the ComStar Schism and Word of Blake's relocation to Gibson, Blakist forces became major Cicada users, eventually rivaling the FWLM in numbers deployed.

The Jihad's devastation of Gibson seemed to doom the Cicada once more, but Andurien AeroTech's decision to split from the Blakist-tainted FWDI led to the establishment of Westover BattleMechs. This new subsidiary refurbished an abandoned FWDI facility on Westover, resuming Cicada production and introducing modern variants incorporating variable-speed pulse technology and re-engineered lasers for the reunified Free Worlds League's forces.
BMCicada_A.deployment: The first Cicada variant produced by Westover BattleMechs following the Jihad, this variant represents the design's evolution for the ilClan era. This configuration mounts medium variable-speed pulse lasers in each side torso alongside a center-mounted medium re-engineered laser, providing accurate firepower effective against both conventional and hardened targets. An engine-mounted supercharger allows brief bursts of exceptional speed, restoring some of the mobility that made the original Cicada famous while ferro-fibrous armor and endo-steel construction maximize protection within the forty-ton frame.

BMFirestarter_A.overview:
The Firestarter was originally designed by Argile Technologies of Skye in 2550 as a specialized incendiary assault platform. The definitive FS9-H variant debuted in 2703 and quickly became the standard against which all incendiary 'Mechs were measured, with nearly three thousand units seeing active service by the onset of the Amaris Civil War in 2776. The design's popularity ensured continued production through the Succession Wars, with Argile maintaining manufacturing until the catastrophic destruction of their plant and headquarters during the Third Succession War. Coventry Metal Works assumed full production in 2895 when Argile declined to rebuild their facilities.

The Firestarter's specialized role as an indirect assault unit, combined with its robust parts availability, has made it a staple of reconnaissance and garrison forces across the Inner Sphere for centuries.
BMFirestarter_A.capabilities:
The Firestarter was rarely attached to front-line lances, instead being assigned at the company or regimental level where commanders could deploy it to support attack groups or scout wooded terrain. While capable of threatening other light 'Mechs, the design's specified loadout of four Purity L-Series flamers, two Deprus RF machine guns, and two Magna Mk II medium lasers can do little against the formidable armor and weaponry of medium and heavy opponents.

The ability to set fires made the FS9 invaluable as a supporting 'Mech, as skillfully placed blazes could rout enemy forces, break lines, and corner 'Mechs, not to mention threaten even the biggest tanks with a fiery demise. An entire series of tactics was developed around creating and spreading wildfires, with Firestarter pilots particularly fond of setting dense woods afire while enemy 'Mechs advance through them, or igniting buildings sheltering enemy units.

Protected by five and a half tons of Livingston Ceramics armor and capable of jumping 180 meters with its six Luxor Load Lifters jump jets, the Firestarter could also create fire and smoke to cover a retreat and hamper pursuit. The design also works well as a scout, its speed and maneuverability providing decent field protection while clearing wooded areas that enemies might use for ambushes.
BMFirestarter_A.history:
Since Firestarters were common in all 'Mech forces before the Succession Wars, none of the five Successor States suffered a shortage of these 'Mechs in the early conflicts. In the earliest days of the First Succession War, the Second Lyran Guard was assigned to garrison the planet of Port Moseby, a vitally important trade center. In August 2789, House Kurita's Second Arkab Legion attacked, landing elements near the capital city despite aerospace fighter opposition. The invaders advanced through heavily wooded country toward the capital, and defending Firestarters were sent to intercept.

An intense drought had left the forests tinder-dry, and the Firestarters quickly ringed the Kurita forces in flames. While the enemy 'Mechs struggled through the burning forest, the defenders brought their forces to the edge of the fire, engaging each 'Mech as it stumbled from the inferno. The Kurita forces were forced to retreat, having suffered significant losses. This engagement enhanced the prestige of the Firestarter and demonstrated the design's ability to transform entire battlefields into wastelands, prompting commanders to experiment with various deployment methods including dedicated incendiary lances.

Firestarters were also primarily responsible for scorched-earth missions carried out in the early days of the Succession Wars. On the modern battlefield, however, that tactic is extremely rare, used only when long-term victory is impossible or when a target is too valuable to fall into enemy hands. After the Fourth Succession War, many Firestarters were incorporated into light and even medium 'Mech lances to replace more costly units that had been destroyed or taken out of action.

The Federated Commonwealth unveiled the FS9-S in 3049, featuring recovered lostech to enhance scouting capabilities. This evolution continued with Luthien Armor Works' development of an OmniMech conversion, while both Coventry Metal Works and Defiance Industries have manufactured variants through the Dark Age era, ensuring the Firestarter's continued relevance on battlefields across the Inner Sphere.
BMFirestarter_A.deployment: A Defiance Industries refresh of the Firestarter based on their Jihad-era experimental FS9-X81 project, this variant has sparked ongoing legal action from Coventry Metal Works over the "Mirage" name. Turning to Clan technology to overcome the developmental issues that plagued the prototype, the design features classic styling built around a Clan-grade XL engine, endo-composite chassis, and reflective armor. The centerpiece is a Clan Sea Fox-supplied plasma cannon supplemented by Clan ER medium and ER small lasers, while arm-mounted and rear-facing flamers retain traditional incendiary capability for both House and mercenary markets.

BMMercury_A.overview:
The Mercury was introduced in 2742 as a next-generation light reconnaissance BattleMech intended to replace the aging Stinger and Wasp designs within the Star League Defense Force. Designed and manufactured by Mitchell Vehicles, the Mercury represented a bold leap forward in light 'Mech philosophy, combining superior speed, enhanced firepower, and innovative construction techniques into a twenty-ton frame without sacrificing armor protection. The design's most revolutionary feature was its modular weapon replacement system, which allowed damaged components to be swapped out in minutes rather than hours, drastically reducing maintenance overhead in the field.

Restricted exclusively to SLDF formations, the Mercury never saw widespread distribution among the Great Houses. Following the Amaris Civil War and the subsequent Exodus, virtually all surviving Mercury units departed the Inner Sphere with General Kerensky's forces. The few that remained were gradually lost during the Succession Wars as irreplaceable components failed and factories were destroyed. The design was believed extinct until ComStar revealed stockpiled examples when it unveiled the Com Guards in the early thirty-first century, eventually restarting production lines on Terra to sustain this venerable scout through the Clan Invasion, the Jihad, and beyond.
BMMercury_A.capabilities:
The heart of the Mercury is its Myomer Acceleration Signal Circuitry system, which acts as a turbocharger for the 'Mech's myomer bundles. In combination with an LTV 160 fusion engine, the MASC system allows the Mercury to achieve momentary bursts of speed approaching 172 kilometers per hour, making it one of the fastest light 'Mechs ever fielded. While prolonged use risks damage to the leg actuators, these bursts of speed are often the critical difference between survival and destruction for a scout operating behind enemy lines. Three tons of Mitchell-091 Ferro-Fibrous armor provide superior protection compared to most twenty-ton contemporaries, allowing the Mercury to absorb hits that would cripple a Stinger or Wasp.

The Mercury's armament consists of two Martell medium lasers and two Hessen IX small lasers, an all-energy loadout that gives the 'Mech excellent endurance on extended patrols. The small lasers in the head and center torso feature the design's signature modular replacement system, using plug-and-fight technology that allows technicians to unbolt and replace an entire weapon assembly in minutes. Critics of the design have consistently pointed to the Mercury's lack of jump jets as its primary weakness, limiting its ability to navigate rough terrain. Despite this drawback, Star League commanders widely accepted the trade-off, as the Mercury's speed and heavier armor allowed it to survive longer in sustained engagements than comparable scouts.
BMMercury_A.history:
The Mercury's debut in 2742 was met with considerable fanfare, with Mitchell Vehicles describing multiple breakthrough systems in general terms while keeping specifics closely guarded. The design was restricted entirely to the SLDF Regular Army, with units stationed primarily on Terra and at the Graham IV production facility. When General Kerensky launched the Exodus, all Mercury-equipped formations departed with him, stranding only a handful of the 'Mechs in the Inner Sphere.

Those few Mercurys left behind faced a slow decline during the Succession Wars. The highest concentration belonged to the Eighth Recon Battalion of the Third Regimental Combat Team, which fielded twelve of the machines before losing all of them during fighting on Sendai in 2798. BMValkyrie_A.overview:
The Valkyrie was originally planned for use by the Star League Defense Force, but production did not begin until 2787 due to legal disputes with Harvard Company, Inc., who claimed the design was a copy of the Wasp LAM. This delay meant the light BattleMech entered service after the fall of the Star League, during the First Succession War. Because all Corean Enterprises facilities producing the Valkyrie were located within Federated Suns space, the design became exclusive property of House Davion for centuries.

The Valkyrie filled a unique niche as a light fire-support 'Mech, replacing the lighter Wasp and Stinger designs in crack combat regiments. Its combination of long-range missile firepower and heavier armor earned it a fearsome reputation among enemy MechWarriors, who learned that once a Valkyrie attacks, "it stays with you until either you drop or it does."
BMValkyrie_A.capabilities:
The Valkyrie carries a Devastator Series-07 LRM-10 launcher as its primary weapon, an unusual choice for a light 'Mech that gives it striking power unmatched by most designs in its weight class. Though limited to only twelve reloads, roughly two minutes of continuous fire, the missile system allows Valkyrie pilots to engage targets at ranges where most light 'Mechs cannot respond effectively. A Sutel IX medium laser mounted in the right arm provides close-range backup, allowing the 'Mech to finish off targets softened by missile fire.

Eleven single heat sinks allow the Valkyrie to maintain a high rate of fire while jumping frequently without risking overheating. Five jump jets propel the 'Mech up to 150 meters at a time, compensating for its relatively modest top speed of 86.4 kilometers per hour. Six tons of armor, twice that carried by either the Wasp or Stinger, enables the Valkyrie to absorb punishment that would cripple lighter scouts.

This design philosophy sacrifices raw speed for staying power, making the Valkyrie most effective as a lance support element rather than a solo skirmisher. The flat potential damage curve means the 'Mech is equally dangerous at extended range or close quarters, and experienced pilots are often assigned to Valkyries in recognition of their value on the battlefield.
BMValkyrie_A.history:
Production of the Valkyrie began in 2787 at Corean Enterprises' automated facility on New Avalon, one of the few surviving fully-automated BattleMech factories from the Star League era. Despite the technological decline of the Succession Wars, the facility maintained a steady output of 130 units annually, reaching nearly 200 during the desperate fighting of the First Succession War. The design quickly became the standard light 'Mech of the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, with every regiment and nearly every battalion fielding at least one Valkyrie.

Archon Katrina Steiner helped Defiance Industries strike a licensing deal with Corean during the alliance between their realms, expanding production to Hesperus II. However, the Fourth Succession War brought a significant setback when the Draconis Combine captured Marduk, home of Norse BattleMech Works and supplier of the Valkyrie's jump jets. Corean eventually resolved the shortage by switching to HildCo Interplanetary's Model 12 jump jets.

Following the formation of the Federated Commonwealth, the Valkyrie was selected as a standard light 'Mech for the unified military, and the discovery of the Helm Memory Core allowed NAIS to restore the New Avalon facility to its full Star League production capacity. The upgraded VLK-QD entered service in 3049, incorporating endo steel construction and improved electronics.

The FedCom Civil War devastated Davion light 'Mech forces, and Valkyrie production halted when HildCo ceased supplying jump jets after the St. Ives Compact fell to the Capellan Confederation. Vicore Industries provided a solution through secretly negotiated manufacturing rights for HildCo jump jets, leading to new production facilities on Demeter and upgraded variants reaching frontline units by July 3067. The Word of Blake occupation of New Avalon severely damaged the automated factory, which remained offline for more than a decade.

By the thirty-second century, the Valkyrie had spread throughout the Inner Sphere through battle losses and expanded licensing. Clan Wolf's capture of Stewart in 3134 led to the development of a mixed-technology Clan variant for solahma forces after a successful Trial of Possession against Clan Sea Fox on the moon of Clyde. The design remains emblematic of the Federated Suns, where Valkyries have protected critical commanders, including Regent Erik Sandoval-Groell during the fall of Palmyra in 3144, and turned the tide in desperate defensive actions across centuries of warfare.
BMValkyrie_A.deployment: Developed by Clan Wolf after they secured control of Stewart in 3138, the Valkyrie C is a mixed-technology variant designed for solahma troops and export. The 'Mech uses an Inner Sphere XL engine and XL gyro combined with improved jump jets, allowing it to cover 240 meters in a single jump while maintaining good ground speed. Armament consists of a Clan-built medium pulse laser and Clan LRM-10 with two tons of ammunition, providing firepower superior to most Inner Sphere light 'Mechs. Clan CASE II protects the ammunition bay, and Clan ferro-fibrous armor provides excellent protection for the weight. Following a Trial of Possession on the moon of Clyde, Clan Sea Fox acquired limited rights to a percentage of yearly production output.

Production of the Valkyrie began in 2787 at Corean Enterprises' automated facility on New Avalon, one of the few surviving fully-automated BattleMech factories from the Star League era. Despite the technological decline of the Succession Wars, the facility maintained a steady output of 130 units annually, reaching nearly 200 during the desperate fighting of the First Succession War. The design quickly became the standard light 'Mech of the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, with every regiment and nearly every battalion fielding at least one Valkyrie.

Archon Katrina Steiner helped Defiance Industries strike a licensing deal with Corean during the alliance between their realms, expanding production to Hesperus II. However, the Fourth Succession War brought a significant setback when the Draconis Combine captured Marduk, home of Norse BattleMech Works and supplier of the Valkyrie's jump jets. Corean eventually resolved the shortage by switching to HildCo Interplanetary's Model 12 jump jets.

Following the formation of the Federated Commonwealth, the Valkyrie was selected as a standard light 'Mech for the unified military, and the discovery of the Helm Memory Core allowed NAIS to restore the New Avalon facility to its full Star League production capacity. The upgraded VLK-QD entered service in 3049, incorporating endo steel construction and improved electronics.

The FedCom Civil War devastated Davion light 'Mech forces, and Valkyrie production halted when HildCo ceased supplying jump jets after the St. Ives Compact fell to the Capellan Confederation. Vicore Industries provided a solution through secretly negotiated manufacturing rights for HildCo jump jets, leading to new production facilities on Demeter and upgraded variants reaching frontline units by July 3067. The Word of Blake occupation of New Avalon severely damaged the automated factory, which remained offline for more than a decade.

By the thirty-second century, the Valkyrie had spread throughout the Inner Sphere through battle losses and expanded licensing. Clan Wolf's capture of Stewart in 3134 led to the development of a mixed-technology Clan variant for solahma forces after a successful Trial of Possession against Clan Sea Fox on the moon of Clyde. The design remains emblematic of the Federated Suns, where Valkyries have protected critical commanders, including Regent Erik Sandoval-Groell during the fall of Palmyra in 3144, and turned the tide in desperate defensive actions across centuries of warfare.
BMValkyrie_B.deployment: Developed by Clan Wolf after they secured control of Stewart in 3138, the Valkyrie C is a mixed-technology variant designed for solahma troops and export. The 'Mech uses an Inner Sphere XL engine and XL gyro combined with improved jump jets, allowing it to cover 240 meters in a single jump while maintaining good ground speed. Armament consists of a Clan-built medium pulse laser and Clan LRM-10 with two tons of ammunition, providing firepower superior to most Inner Sphere light 'Mechs. Clan CASE II protects the ammunition bay, and Clan ferro-fibrous armor provides excellent protection for the weight. Following a Trial of Possession on the moon of Clyde, Clan Sea Fox acquired limited rights to a percentage of yearly production output.

BMValkyrie_Prime.overview:
The Valkyrie was originally planned for use by the Star League Defense Force, but production did not begin until 2787 due to legal disputes with Harvard Company, Inc., who claimed the design was a copy of the Wasp LAM. This delay meant the light BattleMech entered service after the fall of the Star League, during the First Succession War. Because all Corean Enterprises facilities producing the Valkyrie were located within Federated Suns space, the design became exclusive property of House Davion for centuries.

The Valkyrie filled a unique niche as a light fire-support 'Mech, replacing the lighter Wasp and Stinger designs in crack combat regiments. Its combination of long-range missile firepower and heavier armor earned it a fearsome reputation among enemy MechWarriors, who learned that once a Valkyrie attacks, "it stays with you until either you drop or it does."
BMValkyrie_Prime.capabilities:
The Valkyrie carries a Devastator Series-07 LRM-10 launcher as its primary weapon, an unusual choice for a light 'Mech that gives it striking power unmatched by most designs in its weight class. Though limited to only twelve reloads, roughly two minutes of continuous fire, the missile system allows Valkyrie pilots to engage targets at ranges where most light 'Mechs cannot respond effectively. A Sutel IX medium laser mounted in the right arm provides close-range backup, allowing the 'Mech to finish off targets softened by missile fire.

Eleven single heat sinks allow the Valkyrie to maintain a high rate of fire while jumping frequently without risking overheating. Five jump jets propel the 'Mech up to 150 meters at a time, compensating for its relatively modest top speed of 86.4 kilometers per hour. Six tons of armor, twice that carried by either the Wasp or Stinger, enables the Valkyrie to absorb punishment that would cripple lighter scouts.

This design philosophy sacrifices raw speed for staying power, making the Valkyrie most effective as a lance support element rather than a solo skirmisher. The flat potential damage curve means the 'Mech is equally dangerous at extended range or close quarters, and experienced pilots are often assigned to Valkyries in recognition of their value on the battlefield.
